title: EMG-Based Adaptation of Anisotropic Virtual Fixtures for Robot-Assisted Surgical Resection and Dissection
summary: In this paper, we address the development of an adaptive assistance system for robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery, specifically for delicate tasks such as Resection and Dissection. Even if Virtual Fixtures offer significant advantages for guiding a surgeon's movements, conventional Virtual Fixtures are often defined by fixed geometries, lacking the flexibility to adapt to the surgical workflow or the surgeon's immediate intent. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for an adaptive and anisotropic virtual fixture. In addition, we introduce an intuitive control interface that modulates the fixture's geometry in real-time based on the surgeon's intent, inferred from EMG signals. This approach allows the surgeon to dynamically expand or disengage the constraint by contracting their forearm muscles, enabling seamless transitions between precise guided motion and free repositioning of the tool. Experimental results from a pilot user study, based on a standardized surgical training task, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The system showed significant improvements in task accuracy and movement consistency, alongside a reduction in perceived cognitive load, effort, and frustration.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive anisotropic virtual fixture framework for robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery that uses EMG signals to infer surgeon intent and dynamically adjust constraint geometry, improving task accuracy and reducing cognitive load.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于机器人辅助腹腔镜手术的自适应各向异性虚拟夹具框架，通过EMG信号推断外科医生意图并动态调整约束几何形状，提高了任务精度并降低了认知负荷。
summary_zh: 本文针对机器人辅助腹腔镜手术中的自适应辅助系统开发进行了研究，特别聚焦于切除与解剖等精细操作任务。尽管虚拟夹具为引导外科医生操作提供了显著优势，但传统虚拟夹具通常由固定几何形状定义，缺乏适应手术流程或医生即时意图的灵活性。为克服这些局限，我们提出了一种新型自适应各向异性虚拟夹具框架。此外，我们引入了一个直观的控制界面，该界面通过从肌电信号推断医生的操作意图，实时调整夹具的几何形态。该方法允许医生通过收缩前臂肌肉动态扩展或解除约束，从而在精确引导运动和工具自由重新定位之间实现无缝切换。基于标准化手术训练任务的初步用户研究实验结果表明，所提方法具有良好的有效性。该系统在任务精度和运动一致性方面显著提升，同时降低了感知认知负荷、努力程度和挫败感。

title: Point-Wise Geometry-Aware Transformer for Partial-to-Full Point Cloud Registration in Computer-Assisted Surgery
summary: Partial-to-full registration remains challenging due to varying overlap ratios, fluctuating point densities, and the presence of noise. While transformers have shown strong potential for point cloud processing, prior methods typically confine them to global context aggregation, overlooking fine-grained local geometry crucial for accurate correspondence. We propose \emph{GAPR-Net}, a learning-based point cloud registration framework with a coarse-to-fine architecture that combines convolution and transformer modules, in which local and global information is fused between the partial and full point clouds using a cross-attention mechanism. To achieve this, a transformation-invariant point-wise geometric feature representation is proposed, which can robustly capture relative geometric features for individual points with respect to their neighboring points. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, experiments are conducted on four geometrically distinct bones, including the tibia, femur, pelvis, and thoracic cartilage. The overall registration recall reaches 94.2\%, the method results in a low RMSE of 1.992 mm and $R^2$ values of 0.908 and 0.974 for rotation and translation, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively addresses the partial-to-full point cloud registration problem. The proposed method enables highly accurate 3D point cloud registration using partial observation, providing a critical foundation for precise surgical navigation and robotic interventions in computer-assisted surgery. The code will be accessed after the double-blind review process.
tldr: Proposes GAPR-Net, a coarse-to-fine point cloud registration framework combining convolution and transformer with a transformation-invariant point-wise geometric feature, achieving high accuracy on partial-to-full registration for multiple bones in computer-assisted surgery.
tldr_zh: 提出了GAPR-Net，一种结合卷积和Transformer的粗到细点云配准框架，并引入变换不变的点态几何特征，在计算机辅助手术中对多个骨骼实现了高精度的部分到完整配准。
summary_zh: 摘要：由于重叠率变化、点密度波动以及噪声的存在，部分到整体点云配准仍具有挑战性。尽管Transformer在点云处理中展现出强大潜力，但以往方法通常将其局限于全局上下文聚合，忽略了对于精确对应关系至关重要的细粒度局部几何结构。我们提出\emph{GAPR-Net}，一种基于学习的点云配准框架，采用从粗到细的架构，结合卷积与Transformer模块，并通过交叉注意力机制在部分点云与整体点云之间融合局部和全局信息。为此，我们提出了一种变换不变的点状几何特征表示，能够稳健地捕获每个点相对于其邻域点的相对几何特征。为评估所提方法的有效性，我们在四种几何形态各异的骨骼（包括胫骨、股骨、骨盆和胸软骨）上进行了实验。整体配准召回率达到94.2%，该方法实现了1.992 mm的低均方根误差，旋转和平移的$R^2$值分别为0.908和0.974。结果表明，所提方法有效解决了部分到整体点云配准问题。该方法利用部分观测实现高精度三维点云配准，为计算机辅助手术中的精准手术导航和机器人干预提供了关键基础。代码将在双盲评审后公开。

title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promising reasoning capabilities in general domains, yet their performance remains limited in specialized settings such as healthcare, especially in multilingual and low-resource scenarios. This gap is critical in regions like rural India, where patients often express complex medical queries in native Indic languages and rely on multimodal inputs such as medical images. Existing English-centric MLLMs struggle to support such use cases, limiting equitable access to AI-driven healthcare assistance. To address this challenge, we introduce ArogyaBodha, a large-scale multilingual multimodal medical question-answer dataset constructed from eight heterogeneous sources, covering 31 body systems, six imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains across English and seven major Indian languages. We further propose ArogyaSutra, an actor-critic-based multi-agent framework that integrates tool grounding with dual-memory mechanisms for step-wise, reasoning-aware decision making, and uses stored actor-critic simulation trajectories for distillation. Experiments show that our dataset and framework improve multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations validating the contribution of each component. The source code and dataset are available at: https://iitp-cse.github.io/ ArogyaSutra/
tldr: This paper introduces ArogyaSutra, an actor-critic-based multi-agent framework for multimodal medical reasoning in Indic languages, along with a large-scale multilingual multimodal dataset (ArogyaBodha) to improve healthcare AI accessibility in low-resource regions.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了 ArogyaSutra，一个基于演员-评论家的多智能体框架，用于印度语言的 multimodal 医疗推理，并构建了大规模多语言多模态数据集 ArogyaBodha，旨在提升低资源地区的医疗 AI 可及性。
summary_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在通用领域已展现出具有前景的推理能力，但在医疗保健等专业场景中，尤其在多语言和低资源环境下，其性能仍然有限。这一差距在农村印度等地区尤为关键，当地患者通常以本土印度语言表达复杂的医疗问题，并依赖医学图像等多模态输入。现有以英语为中心的MLLMs难以支持此类用例，从而限制了AI驱动医疗服务的公平可及性。为应对这一挑战，我们引入ArogyaBodha——一个大规模多语言多模态医疗问答数据集，由八个异构来源构建，覆盖31个人体系统、六种成像模态和21个临床领域，涵盖英语及七种主要印度语言。我们进一步提出ArogyaSutra——一个基于演员-评论家的多智能体框架，该框架将工具接地与双记忆机制相结合，实现逐步、推理感知的决策，并利用存储的演员-评论家仿真轨迹进行蒸馏。实验表明，我们的数据集和框架在所有印度语言上均提升了多语言医疗推理的准确性，消融实验验证了每个组件的贡献。源代码和数据集可在以下网址获取：https://iitp-cse.github.io/ArogyaSutra/

title: Deployment-Centered Evaluation: Predicting Query-Level Rejection Risk in a Clinical LLM System
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into clinical systems, making it essential to evaluate the real-world utility of these systems. However, static benchmarks tend to measure correctness rather than user acceptance, aggregate performance across queries, and require densely annotated datasets -- leading to major blind spots for evaluating clinical systems. In this work, we perform a deployment-centered evaluation of an LLM system embedded within electronic health records at an academic medical center, where user feedback is sparse but closely reflects the deployment conditions. Specifically, we train a pre-response classifier that estimates the risk that a future interaction will result in the user rejecting the LLM response, based on query content and deployment-specific context available before generation. We conduct a prospective analysis of our model over 4.5 months of user feedback, finding that our prediction model achieves an AUROC of 0.719. Further, we estimate the benefit of such predictions in two downstream use cases (guardrail triggering and abstention). Our key conceptual insight is that making use of deployment-specific context (i.e., the provider type, department name, language model used for response), as opposed to only query content, improves the ability to predict whether the user will reject the system output. Altogether, our empirical case study demonstrates the feasibility of predicting user rejection using deployment-specific context, opening the door to targeted guardrails.
tldr: This paper presents a deployment-centered evaluation of a clinical LLM system by training a classifier to predict user rejection risk using query content and deployment-specific context (e.g., provider type, department). Over 4.5 months, the model achieved AUROC 0.719, demonstrating feasibility for targeted guardrails.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种以部署为中心的临床LLM系统评估方法，通过训练分类器利用查询内容和部署特定上下文（如提供者类型、科室）预测用户拒绝风险。在4.5个月的评估中，模型AUROC达到0.719，展示了针对性护栏的可行性。
summary_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）正日益融入临床系统，因此评估这些系统的实际效用至关重要。然而，静态基准测试往往侧重于正确性而非用户接受度，会聚合跨查询的性能指标，并且需要密集标注的数据集——这导致了临床系统评估中的重大盲区。在本研究中，我们针对某学术医疗中心电子健康记录中嵌入的LLM系统开展了一项以部署为中心的评估，该场景中的用户反馈稀疏但能紧密反映部署条件。具体而言，我们训练了一个生成前分类器，该分类器基于查询内容及生成前可获取的部署特定上下文，预估未来交互导致用户拒绝LLM响应的风险。我们基于4.5个月的用户反馈对模型进行前瞻性分析，发现预测模型的AUROC达到0.719。此外，我们估算了此类预测在两个下游用例（护栏触发与弃权决策）中的收益。本研究的核心概念洞见在于：相较于仅使用查询内容，利用部署特定上下文（即提供者类型、科室名称、用于生成响应的语言模型）可提升对用户是否会拒绝系统输出的预测能力。总体而言，我们的实证案例研究证明了利用部署特定上下文预测用户拒绝行为的可行性，为定向护栏机制的实现打开了大门。

title: Unified MRI Brain Image Translation via Hierarchical Tumor Structure Comparison
summary:
Multi-modal MRI brain image translation via available modalities holds significant practical importance in modern medicine, providing robust support for early diagnosis, treatment planning, and outcome assessment of diseases. For this purpose, it is important to ensure the fidelity of the tumor regions after translation. However, existing brain image translation methods ignore the structure information of different tumor regions, which could assist translation models in enhancing the quality and clinical applicability of the translated images.
  In this work, we propose a novel translation model called HTSCGAN, which is a unified multi-modal brain image translation generative adversarial model integrating the structural information within tumor regions with the aim of improving the quality of brain image translation. Specifically, the generator employs three Patch Contrast Module (PCM) with different patch sizes to capture the hierarchical structural information of the tumor regions. In addition, a pretrained Patch Classifier (PC) and a pretrained Structure-Aware Encoder (SAE) are employed to derive the generated image containing the same tumor region structure as the ground truth image via patch classification loss and tumor perceptual loss, respectively. The experiments on BraTS2020 and BraTS2021 demonstrate strong performance of our model in both translation tasks and down stream segmentation tasks, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing the quality and clinical relevance of the translated brain images. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HTSCGAN.
tldr: Proposes HTSCGAN, a GAN-based multi-modal MRI brain image translation model that uses hierarchical tumor structure comparison (via patch contrast modules and structure-aware encoders) to improve fidelity of translated tumor regions, validated on BraTS datasets.
tldr_zh: 提出HTSCGAN，一种基于GAN的多模态MRI脑图像翻译模型，通过分层肿瘤结构比较（使用补丁对比模块和结构感知编码器）来提高翻译肿瘤区域的保真度，在BraTS数据集上得到验证。
summary_zh:
多模态MRI脑图像通过可用模态进行翻译在现代医学中具有重要的实际意义，为疾病的早期诊断、治疗规划和疗效评估提供了有力支持。为此，确保翻译后肿瘤区域的保真度至关重要。然而，现有的脑图像翻译方法忽略了不同肿瘤区域的结构信息，而这些信息本可帮助翻译模型提升翻译图像的质量和临床适用性。

在本工作中，我们提出了一种新颖的翻译模型HTSCGAN，这是一个统一的多模态脑图像翻译生成对抗网络，它整合了肿瘤区域内的结构信息，旨在提高脑图像翻译的质量。具体而言，生成器采用三个不同块大小的补丁对比模块（PCM）来捕获肿瘤区域的层次结构信息。此外，利用预训练的补丁分类器（PC）和预训练的结构感知编码器（SAE），通过补丁分类损失和肿瘤感知损失分别生成与真实图像具有相同肿瘤区域结构的图像。在BraTS2020和BraTS2021上的实验表明，我们的模型在翻译任务和下游分割任务中均表现出强劲性能，突显了其在提升翻译脑图像质量和临床相关性方面的有效性。我们的代码可在https://anonymous.4open.science/r/HTSCGAN获取。

title: ffdas: Volumetric ultrasound reconstruction at warp speed
summary: Volumetric ultrafast ultrasound imaging demands reconstruction of images with millions of voxels thousands of times per second, creating computational challenges that limit both real-time feedback and easy offline analysis. Graphics processing units (GPUs) are well suited to this workload, yet we show that standard delay-and-sum implementations underutilize GPU resources through fragmented memory access patterns, even when sufficient computational capacity is available. Three optimization strategies address this: aligning memory access with GPU transfer granularity, halving memory traffic through mixed-precision storage, and exploiting spatial locality to utilize tensor core arithmetic. Together, these achieve kilohertz frame rates for $128^3$-voxel grids with 1024-element arrays, substantially outperforming existing implementations while maintaining image quality. This enables real-time volumetric imaging at scales previously restricted to offline processing, supporting applications such as intraoperative brain imaging and brain-computer interfaces where immediate feedback is essential. We release our implementation as part of the open-source \texttt{ffdas} library.
tldr: This paper presents GPU optimization strategies (memory alignment, mixed-precision, tensor cores) to achieve kilohertz volumetric ultrasound reconstruction, enabling real-time imaging for applications like intraoperative brain imaging and brain-computer interfaces.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了GPU优化策略（内存对齐、混合精度、张量核心），实现了千赫兹体积超声重建，为术中脑成像和脑机接口等应用提供了实时成像能力。
summary_zh: 体积极速超声成像要求每秒数千次重建包含数百万体素的图像，这带来了计算挑战，限制了实时反馈和便捷的离线分析。图形处理器（GPU）非常适合此类工作负载，然而我们表明，标准的延迟求和实现由于碎片化的内存访问模式而未能充分利用GPU资源，即使计算能力充足。针对这一问题，我们提出了三种优化策略：使内存访问与GPU传输粒度对齐、通过混合精度存储将内存流量减半、以及利用空间局部性来使用张量核心算术。这些策略共同实现了使用1024元阵列对$128^3$体素网格进行千赫兹帧率成像，在保持图像质量的同时显著优于现有实现。这使得此前仅限于离线处理的规模能够实现实时体积成像，支持术中脑成像和脑机接口等需要即时反馈的应用。我们将该实现作为开源\texttt{ffdas}库的一部分发布。
